clue.text: Turf hunk out of Britain with tendency for trouble

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

indicators.note: out of says the letter for Britain leaves the word for hunk

parts.note: a slab is a thick hunk of something
B is the abbreviation for Britain (as on car plates)

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts a chunk of turf, apparently prone to causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD's LAW is the British name for the rule that whatever can go wrong will.
explanation.definitionFit: The principle that things will go wrong whenever possible is a supposed natural tendency toward mishap.

clue.text: Changing direction initially, Asian country makes a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: the first letter is a compass direction, north, and it changes to the opposite one, south

parts.note: Nepal is a Himalayan country in Asia

explanation.surface: Nepal changes course and makes a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts enclosing a flower bud, so part of a blooming plant.

clue.text: Papers about musician, say, releasing tango for recorder

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the papers abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: ID papers are identity documents

indicators.note: releasing says the letter for tango is let go

parts.note: a musician is an example of an artist
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Documents concerning a musician dropping the tango from a recorder concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' looks like the instrument beside 'musician', but is someone who writes things down.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist keeps a daily journal, a written record of events.

clue.text: National symbol's a revelation, it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a leak is a revelation of secret information

explanation.surface: A nation's emblem turns out to be a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is the national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh wear this vegetable on St David's Day as their national emblem.

clue.text: Serving, give up point and play without purpose

parts.note: waiting at table is serving
to forgo is to give something up
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: A waiter abandons a point and plays aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Beckett's play, famously one in which nothing happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's absurdist drama has two tramps waiting endlessly for someone who never arrives, so its action seems pointless.

clue.text: Old-fashioned drier whiskey — double!

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ringer (dead ringer) is someone's double

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling for a double whiskey from an old-fashioned barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drier' is the thing that dries: a mangle squeezing water out of washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle with rollers that squeezed water from laundry was the household drying device before spin machines.

clue.text: Darn! Flipping husband entirely rendered powerless in song

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so the word for darn is read upwards

parts.note: to darn is to sew
all means entirely, as in all alone
overcome means overpowered

explanation.surface: A wife exasperated: her flipping husband has been entirely rendered powerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn!' and 'Flipping' look like mild oaths, but are a verb and a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This gospel-derived anthem became the protest anthem of the American civil rights movement.

clue.text: Suggest bottling old wine without any strength

indicators.note: bottling means holding inside, so the suggest word encloses the others

parts.note: to imply is to suggest
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A hint about bottling old wine that has lost its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old word for a dark Spanish wine, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impotently means acting powerlessly, with no force or effect.

clue.text: Sign I'm surprised crossing northerly tracks

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the surprise word goes over the tracks

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: northerly in a down answer means read upwards, so the tracks word is reversed

parts.note: ruts are tracks worn into a road

explanation.surface: A traveller expresses surprise at a sign crossing northbound railway tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture is a movement or action that signals a meaning, a token or signal.

clue.text: Hit a socialist, punching another

indicators.note: punching means going into, so the first socialist ends up inside the second

parts.note: another socialist: a red is a left-winger
Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: One socialist punches another in a political brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a blow beside 'punching', but means arrived at, as in hit a target.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit a figure or a place is to get to it, to arrive.

clue.text: Doves sport with great rook from the east

parts.note: PE is physical education, school sport
ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: in an across answer, reading from the east means right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to rook or skin someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Peace-loving people take up sport with a great bird from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like the bird beside 'Doves', but it is the verb to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves are people favouring peace over war, the opposite of hawks, which is what peaceniks are.

clue.text: Turkish bigwig's yearly investing has bombed

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the yearly letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: PA is per annum, yearly

indicators.note: bombed means failed badly, so the letters of has are scrambled

explanation.surface: An Ottoman grandee's annual investments have failed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'bigwig's' is 'has', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasha was a high-ranking Ottoman official or governor, an important dignitary.

clue.text: Refuge of PM once, saving face

indicators.note: saving here means except, so the face or first letter is left off

parts.note: Tony Blair was the UK Prime Minister 1997-2007

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's hideaway, kept while he tried to save face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving face' reads as preserving dignity but means 'except the front letter'.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den is a hiding place, a refuge where it shelters.

clue.text: Criminal admits that hurt ability to turn a profit

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of admits are bent into a new order

parts.note: ouch is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: A crook confesses that something was painful.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas of Greek legend turned everything he touched into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone said to have this gift makes money from every venture, as Midas made gold.

clue.text: Football club I sense is very bad

parts.note: Aston Villa, the Birmingham football club, is called Villa
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A fan senses that the football club is very bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Villainous means wicked, like a villain, though it can also loosely mean dreadful.

clue.text: Intently watching, but missing a series

indicators.note: missing says the letter a is absent from the word

parts.note: staring is watching intently

explanation.surface: Someone watching closely yet missing part of a TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of events or wins is a run or sequence of them in a row.

clue.text: Ruled about case of snake oil provider

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the ruled word goes round the snake's outer letters

parts.note: ruled paper is lined

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written for its outer letters

explanation.surface: A judge rules on a scandal about snake oil being sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake oil' reads as one phrase; split it, with 'oil provider' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seed is pressed to give linseed oil, used in paints and wood treatments.

clue.text: Guy's partner, one meeting DiCaprio? The earth moved for him!

parts.note: guys and gals go together
I is the Roman numeral one
Leonardo DiCaprio is known as Leo

explanation.surface: A girlfriend meets Leonardo DiCaprio and feels the earth move, a romantic joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The earth moved' is a cliche of passion, but here it is literal: Galileo held that the earth moves round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer championed heliocentrism, insisting our planet orbits the sun rather than standing still.

clue.text: Report composed ought to include partners in play

indicators.note: to include says the rearranged letters take in the partners
composed means put together anew, so the letters of ought are rearranged

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners

explanation.surface: A composed report ought to include the partners in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a bang, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: The report of a gun is the loud bang of its firing.

clue.text: Mythical creature in mythology, tall tale with a twist in the tail?

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge, myth

indicators.text: with a twist in the tail
indicators.note: the end of the word twists, its middle letter moving round to the tail

parts.note: a lie is a tall tale

explanation.surface: A legendary creature from mythology, the kind of tall tale with a twist in its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren whose singing lured sailors onto the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: German legend has a siren on a Rhine rock who lured boatmen to ruin, like a mermaid.

clue.text: Fabric coat from Versace with grim look

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written for its outer letters
to lour (lower) is to frown or look sullen

explanation.surface: A designer coat from Versace worn with a scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Velour is a plush pile cloth like velvet, used for clothing and upholstery.

clue.text: Man in nude possibly could be so described

definitions.text: Man in nude possibly could be so described

indicators.note: in says the man goes inside the rearranged letters
possibly signals that the letters of nude may be arranged differently

parts.note: Rob is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in the nude could well be described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrobed means with one's clothes off, undressed, which is what nude means.

clue.text: Race around dodgy bars with gin in mum's cups

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for race is read backwards

parts.note: to race is to run

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of bars and gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone races round dodgy bars with gin in mum's teacups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum's cups' sounds like crockery, but the cups belong to a breastfeeding mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A bra designed for breastfeeding, with cups that open, is worn by new mothers.

clue.text: Good service, tennis ace

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A good serve from a tennis ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a tennis serve but is a military service.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf, the German player, won 22 Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Rank of Iron Duke, holding appeal up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the iron and duke letters hold the appeal

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: up in a down answer means read upwards, so the appeal word is reversed

parts.note: it is sex appeal

explanation.surface: The rank held by the Iron Duke, Wellington, holding up an appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a military grade but means foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rank smells strongly offensive, as does something fetid.

clue.text: Best to leave a reversing car

indicators.note: reversing means the remaining letters are read backwards
to leave says the letter a departs

parts.note: the cream is the best of something

explanation.surface: It is best to leave a reversing car alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Merc is a familiar short form of Mercedes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merc is a Mercedes-Benz, the German make of motor.

clue.text: Periodical suffering, lumbago's back!

parts.note: hell is great suffering

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of lumbago is used

parts.note: taken as written for its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone's recurring agony: their lumbago, a back complaint, has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: HELLO! is a British celebrity magazine; 'Periodical' looks like 'recurring' but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello! is a weekly magazine, a publication issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Lorna likes men and women with time to make an expected contribution

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel
's bi, short for is bisexual, someone attracted to both men and women

explanation.surface: A woman called Lorna likes men and women, given time to contribute.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Lorna likes men and women' as DOONE'S BI: Lorna is bi.
explanation.definitionFit: To do your bit is an idiom for playing your fair part in a shared effort.

clue.text: Try pirouettes without success in matching clothes

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the twirled word encloses success
pirouettes means spins round, so the letters of the trial word are rearranged

parts.note: to try is to test
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A dancer tries pirouettes in a matching outfit but fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper (sweater) worn together, a classic British women's outfit.

clue.text: In need of cracking fish in desperate need

indicators.note: in says the fish sits inside the jumbled letters
desperate means wild or frantic, so the letters of need are jumbled

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A frantic plea about being in desperate need of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' is decoding a cipher, not breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A coded message is one that has to be deciphered before it can be read.
